analysis: This batch is documentation-only. docs/provider/installation.md head lines 219-256 add the operator-invoked `darkbloom update --rollback` section. The rollback restores the kept predecessor from ~/.darkbloom/recovery/predecessor/ through UpdateInstallLayout.snapshotLiveAsPredecessor, quarantines the rolled-back release, keeps only one predecessor (a second rollback is refused), allows a re-install via --override-quarantine, and refuses while a cluster pair serves. Both files also bump their date lines. docs/provider/troubleshooting.md head lines 151-152 add the rollback cause to the quarantine row and a new 'regresses' row. No source code is in this batch, so no security control changed here. Questions for integration: (1) T-043/TB-003: the rollback authority is the same operator-replaceable binary. The predecessor directory is operator-writable, so restoring from it must re-verify the code signature and the published hashes rather than trust the snapshot; otherwise a tampered predecessor could be installed. Under ADV-001 the operator can already replace the binary, and T-013/T-054 rely on Apple and coordinator code identity rather than local install integrity, so this is mainly a doc/threat-model update question. (2) Downgrade risk: rollback lets a provider run an older release, possibly one later revoked. The coordinator's minimum-version gate and App Attest build qualification/revocation (A-017, T-054) should still reject revoked builds; the provider-side rollback code was not supplied, so this is unverified. (3) T-047 is relevant: the fan helper is not touched by the updater, per the docs. The threat model's T-043 may need updating to mention the manual rollback path. No finding qualifies on documentation evidence alone.
